css:
.mx>i { flex:none; width:6px; border:1.8px solid #2b3a55;
      border-right:none; border-radius:3px 0 0 3px; }

.mx-det>i, .mx-det>i:last-child { width:0; border-left-width:1.7px;
      border-right-width:1.7px; border-top:none; border-bottom:none; border-radius:0; }

/* A DENSE MATRIX STEPS DOWN ONE SIZE, AND ONLY A DENSE ONE.
   A 3x3 whose cells hold `21 - 30 + 7 + 2` needs about 148px a cell
   at 18px; a 440px column leaves 140px once the gaps and rules are
   paid for, so the cell wrapped mid-sum. Shrinking EVERY matrix to
   fix that is what makes a short `[1 2; 3 4]` look tiny beside its
   neighbours, so the step is scoped to the matrices that earn it --
   see `_DENSE_CELL` in format/matrix.py. 16px prints at 11.74px,
   clear of the 11px floor; 15px would print at 11.01px and still not
   fit, which is why the step stops here rather than going smaller. */
.mx-dense>.mxg>span { font-size:16px; }
.mx-dense>.mxg { gap:6px 11px; padding:5px 8px; }
